evals.prompt: Add a new shared statistical estimator to statgpu. Start with the simplest correct implementation.
evals.expected_output: The workflow treats NumPy, CuPy, and Torch as the default completion contract for a genuinely new shared numerical capability, while allowing CPU-first as an intermediate implementation rather than declaring it complete.
assertions: The plan includes NumPy, CuPy, and Torch closure or an explicit approved narrower contract/deferral.
A CPU-only first step is not labeled COMPLETE.

evals.prompt: Deprecate one constructor parameter without changing numerical dispatch or results.
evals.expected_output: The workflow keeps scope on API compatibility, warnings, clone/get_params/set_params and targeted regressions instead of opening unrelated GPU, inference or CV implementation work.
assertions: The response treats the task as API/deprecation work.
The response does not require new backend implementations merely because the estimator has GPU support.
The response checks omission versus explicit legacy defaults and sklearn-style reconstruction where applicable.

evals.prompt: Expose a new tunable loss x penalty combination in the public penalized-model API.
evals.expected_output: The workflow includes direct fit plus CV path/grid/folds/scoring/selection/final-refit closure by default and does not allow the first implementation to avoid CV simply by omitting the claim.
assertions: Direct fit and CV are both part of the default completion contract.
Any CV deferral is explicit rather than implied by omission.

evals.prompt: The generic penalized base already has an inference implementation, but typed wrappers, constructor defaults, result metadata, and docs disagree about which method is actually used. Repair the interface without inventing a new numerical algorithm.
evals.expected_output: The workflow classifies this as existing capability reconciliation/public contract repair, performs contract reconnaissance and a consumer graph before production edits, traces requested -> resolved -> reported inference identity, preserves already-correct numerical paths, and closes affected wrappers/CV/formula/docs rather than treating the task as a brand-new numerical feature.
assertions: A current capability matrix is built before production edits.
Shared-base consumers such as typed wrappers and meta-estimators are inventoried.
Requested, resolved, and reported inference method identity is explicitly frozen.
Already-correct numerical implementations are preserved rather than needlessly reimplemented.

evals.prompt: A helper is documented as a generic GLM bootstrap fallback, but its implementation resamples Gaussian residuals and reconstructs a penalized linear L1 model for every refit. Make the public inference contract correct.
evals.expected_output: The workflow treats resampling validity as a blocking inference contract, inventories the claimed families and refit identity, defines family/model-valid DGP and selection/tuning semantics, and either narrows/fail-closes the unsupported scope or implements a valid family-aware path before calling it generic.
assertions: The response checks resampling unit/DGP and refit estimator family/penalty.
The response does not accept a Gaussian-Lasso residual bootstrap as a universal GLM fallback.
Unsupported combinations fail closed unless a valid implementation is added.

evals.prompt: A new public behavior is implemented on master while the latest published package is 0.2.5 and the intended next release is 0.2.6. Finish the feature workflow and documentation.
evals.expected_output: The workflow distinguishes current published 0.2.5 from behavior implemented on master and targeted for 0.2.6, updates final docs before the independent review, avoids an unrelated premature package-version bump, and performs exact-head evidence closure after all review fixes/docs commits.
assertions: The docs describe 0.2.6 as targeted/planned rather than already released.
Documentation precedes the final independent review.
The final evidence/CI/review claims are rechecked against the exact final head.
